name: Claude Managed Agents: Dreaming, Outcomes & Multi-Agent Orchestration
hook: Three major upgrades to Claude Managed Agents shipped at Code with Claude SF (May 6). Dreaming (research preview) — a scheduled background process reviews past agent sessions, extracts recurring patterns, and curates memory so agents self-improve between runs; users control whether updates apply automatically or require review. Outcomes (public beta) — write a plain-English success rubric; a separate Claude instance grades the output in isolation from the agent's reasoning trace; internal benchmarks show +10 percentage-point task success on the hardest tasks. Multi-Agent Orchestration (public beta) — a lead agent assigns sub-tasks to parallel sub-agents on a shared filesystem, all traceable in the Claude Console. Covered within 24 hours by SD Times, Digital Trends, SiliconANGLE, The Decoder, The New Stack, CryptoBriefing, 9to5Mac, and US News.

name: Claude Code Rate Limits 2× + SpaceX Compute Deal

name: Claude Code on Desktop (New Native Surface)
hook: Announced at Code with Claude SF (May 6): the third Claude Code surface after CLI and IDE extensions. A native desktop application designed for users who want a full-screen GUI with live preview, image rendering, and rich formatted outputs rather than a terminal-split experience. Anthropic also foregrounded /ultrareview at the event — the public-research-preview fleet of cloud bug-hunting agents that land findings in your CLI or Desktop — as a headline workflow for the Desktop surface. Designed for the 'I want visual results, not scrolling terminal output' audience.

name: Claude Code v2.1.132 (May 6, post-conference)
hook: `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` is now injected into every Bash tool subprocess environment — enables audit-trail hooks to correlate every shell command to its originating session without manual instrumentation. `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ALTERNATE_SCREEN=1` lets terminals that mishandle the fullscreen renderer opt out. Critical fixes: unbounded memory growth with MCP stdio servers (high-priority for long-running MCP sessions); parallel shell tool calls no longer cancel sibling reads when one fails; NFD-accented characters no longer corrupt in vim mode; pasting text starting with `/` no longer silently swallows input.

name: claude-code-ultimate-guide (FlorianBruniaux)
hook: Updated May 4 — 24K+ lines across 16 specialized guides from beginner to power user. Standout: 181 production-ready templates packaged as installable Claude Code plugins (security, DevOps, release automation, code quality, PR workflows); a 271-question knowledge-validation quiz; 48 Mermaid diagrams; and a 655-entry malicious-skills database alongside 28 CVE notes in a threat-modeling guide — the only community-maintained catalog tracking deliberately harmful Claude Code skills, especially timely alongside the Mitiga MCP disclosure this week.

name: claude-code-mcp (steipete)
hook: ~1.1k stars, by Peter Steinberger (@steipete). Exposes Claude Code as a single `claude_code` MCP tool so any parent AI — Claude Desktop, another Claude Code instance, a Managed Agent workflow — can spawn Claude Code as a sub-agent with all permission prompts bypassed for one-shot execution. The 'agent in your agent' pattern becomes a first-class citizen today with Anthropic's Multi-Agent Orchestration entering public beta; claude-code-mcp lets you replicate the pattern in any MCP-compatible runtime without waiting for managed infrastructure. A community-enhanced fork (`grahama1970/claude-code-mcp-enhanced`) adds orchestration capabilities and self-contained execution patterns.

name: MCP Token Theft via ~/.claude.json — Mitiga Research
hook: Mitiga security researchers disclosed a MitM attack chain against Claude Code's MCP subsystem: inject a malicious entry into `~/.claude.json`, silently redirect MCP traffic, capture OAuth tokens for connected SaaS platforms, and maintain persistent access with no visible indicator to the user. Reported to Anthropic on April 10, 2026; Anthropic responded April 12 — 'out of scope.' Covered by SecurityWeek and circulating on HN. Practical takeaway: audit your `~/.claude.json` MCP server entries, especially after installing skills or plugins from unknown sources.
